subject.title: [Feature] Cron and subagent sessions lack user context for plugin OAuth tools

question: Should OpenClaw add a generic requester-identity contract for unattended cron and sessions_spawn plugin OAuth tools, and which identity fields may those runs expose?
rationale: This would change plugin-visible OAuth authority for scheduled and spawned execution, so automation cannot safely choose the product API shape or security posture.

options.title: Design Generic Requester Context
options.body: Add a typed runtime and Plugin SDK seam for explicit requester identity, including consent, audit, revocation, privacy, and concurrency rules before implementation.

options.title: Keep It Plugin-Owned For Now
options.body: Ask affected plugins to use plugin-local scheduled identity configuration while core avoids a generic unattended requester API.

options.title: Defer Pending Live Proof
options.body: Keep cron and spawned runs headless until maintainers have live evidence from more OAuth-dependent plugins and can scope the contract narrowly.

recommendation.title: Design Generic Requester Context
recommendation.body: Add a typed runtime and Plugin SDK seam for explicit requester identity, including consent, audit, revocation, privacy, and concurrency rules before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history across cron, sessions/subagent, and plugin requester identity work in the affected boundary.
